The Portland Trail Blazers stayed hot on Friday night, defeating the Golden State Warriors 116-94 at Moda Center to improve to 13-6 on the season. That win officially secured West Group C for Portland, which will advance to the knockout stage of the NBA Cup.

The Blazers continue to establish themselves as one of the better teams in the Western Conference and will have an opportunity to further prove that in the knockout stage of the NBA Cup.

#2675. Steelers players express support for Mike McCarthy after winning first game since Aaron Rodgers divorce

It can't be denied the Pittsburgh Steelers are a different team after one of the most eventful weeks of the season, but that apparently isn't all bad.

A number of Steelers players expressed their support for head coach Mike McCarthy in the aftermath of a 27-5 win over the Denver Broncos on Black Friday, the team's first game since a very public divorce with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

The saga saw Rodgers make several claims while appearing on "The Pat McAfee Show" that painted McCarthy as disconnected at best and dangerously incompetent at worst after the Steelers benched him, and shortly before they released him. It's a situation with a little precedent in the NFL, and it led to all eyes on McCarthy and the Steelers in Week 12.

Behind the scenes, there was plenty of talking. James Palmer of NFL Network reported before the game that the team's leadership council — a group of veteran players who regularly meet with McCarthy — met on Wednesday and held an "airing of grievances" to address some of the stuff Rodgers was talking about. The meeting reportedly left McCarthy "humbled," but also allowed him to explain to the players why he handled everything the way he did.

The meeting apparently left the team on firmer footing, with Steelers cornerback Jalen Ramsey saying the team expressed its support to McCarthy:

"For the past couple days, we as players, we were like, 'Coach, you good.' Let us turn this up, let us get in our zone."

Quarterback Mason Rudolph, Rodgers' replacement under center, also said the players were behind McCarthy:

"I think the leadership council rallied around coach McCarthy. I think in a weird way, the adversity probably brought us closer together. We've just got to keep carrying that in week to week."

McCarthy, meanwhile, seemed happy with how the team responded:

"Everything that was discussed was healthy. Lot of things in there, but what came out of it was urgency. I thought our leaders did a tremendous job of bringing the urgency to their rooms and it definitely showed up."

One particular point of criticism from Rodgers was that McCarthy had allegedly spent little time engaging with the Pittsburgh defense, despite the quarterback advising that he should. McCarthy's background is almost purely on the offense and he's well known to prioritize that side of the ball while leaving the rest to his defensive coordinator.

McCarthy actually admitted Rodgers was right about his lack of focus on the defense:

"I have not spent enough time with the defense. That's something as far as job responsibility, job description, these are things that will be looked at in the offseason, but it's a point where in our year, we're making adjustments. Definitely conscientious of it."

Steelers defensive end T.J. Watt indicated the players spoke to McCarthy about that, and the results were encouraging:

"Mike just admitted that he has got to spend some more time with the defense. We've had a lot of really good conversations, especially recently, and look forward to continuing to build off of what you saw tonight."

Mike McCarthy had a tough week, but got a win.

The Steelers veterans also had plenty of praise for Rudolph, whose experience with the team goes back to 2018. Watt didn't seem surprised he was ready for the game:

"Mason Rudolph is a true professional. He's been a true professional since I've known him. A guy that's trained like the starter no matter how long he's been here, whether he's the backup or the starter. We have extreme belief in him and he's a great locker room glue guy."

Rudolph didn't exactly light up the scoreboard against Denver, but he was at least efficient, going 9-for-15 for 142 yards, 1 touchdown and 0 interceptions. It was a run-heavy game script with the Steelers leading 14-0 after the first quarter and by multiple scores for the rest of the game.

Still, Steelers defensive tackle Cameron Heyward noticed Rudolph doing what was needed:

"He's ready for all those moments. He understand that with everything that went on, he couldn't have a drop-off. I'm just appreciative to have a guy who when s*** hits the fan, he's able to say, 'Alright, I've gotta step up.'"

It was a strong performance at least compared to, well, the standard Rodgers set during the season. NFL Network's Michael Florio noted his 0.19 EPA per dropback, an advanced stat measuring offensive efficiency, was the second-best mark by a Steelers quarterback all season. Rodgers exceeded that level only once all season, in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals.

McCarthy did at one point go out of his way to note "I'm the offensive play-caller," a notable statement given that Rodgers reportedly gave the Steelers an ultimatum that the team give him offensive play-calling duties or release him.

However, he seemed far more interested in moving on with the team as constructed, and said he was grateful for the response to a turbulent week:

"There's a lot going on. Anytime you're in a situation where time is taken away from winning and your team responds, it is extremely important and gratifying. The reality of this game — and it will always be as far as my approach — this is a players' game. We have a very important role in this sport, but you have to make sure you keep it about the players. We still have work to do from my position and we'll continue to do that. We've just got to keep building off things that we've done well.

"We got the win today. It was definitely a hard travel week for us as a football team. I'm proud of our players. I'm proud of our coaching staff. I'm proud of our support staff and I really appreciate all the other support."

Meanwhile, Rodgers, passed along his own thoughts via Al Michaels during the game.

The Atlanta Hawks were in Boston on Friday night to face the Celtics. It was a big game for both teams regarding the NBA Cup, and the objective was clear: win and you advance to the knockout round. There could be some other things that could happen for the Hawks to get in if they lost, but winning would make everything better for them.

The Hawks had all of their main guys available for the game, with CJ McCollum, Jock Landale, Asa Newell and Mouhamed Gueye still out. For the Celtics, Mitchell Robinson was out with an illness.

Offense was hard to come by from both teams to start the game, and the only thing the Hawks had to show for it was a 3-pointer from Dyson Daniels.

The good news for the Hawks is that the Celtics couldn't get much going either, and the score stayed 8-3 for some time. Both teams started to heat up just a little as the quarter continued, but the Hawks still found themselves fighting from behind.

Lu Dort came in off the bench and was aggressive for the Hawks, and he led the team in points in the quarter.

Outside Dort and Daniels, Jalen Johnson was the only other player for the Hawks who scored in the quarter. The Hawks shot 5-of-23 from the field and 1-of-14 from the 3-point line. Going into the second, the Hawks trailed 29-14.

The Hawks never let the game get too out of hand, and they had several chances to get it within double digits, but the shots just weren't falling. When the shots weren't falling, Johnson used his physicality to make things happen in the paint.

The Hawks were able to keep things interesting going into halftime despite the poor shooting, and they trailed the Celtics 51-39.

The Hawks then cut down their deficit to single digits after this 3-pointer from Johnson.

The second unit that has been strong for the Hawks over their last few games was able to keep the momentum going and keep cutting their deficit.

It was a good way to end the quarter, and they came out with their first lead of the game. Going into the fourth, the Hawks led 70-69. The second unit continued to play well going into the fourth, and Dort hit a deep 3-pointer to give the Hawks the lead.

There's no doubt that this game got physical down the stretch, and it affected both teams on the offensive end. Points were hard to come by, which meant every possession was important.

Putting the ball in Daniels' hands was a good idea down the stretch because he was able to find Johnson for this dunk.

With less than almost a minute remaining, the game was tied at 83. Alexander-Walker broke the tie with a layup to give the Hawks a two-point lead, and on the other end, Johnson got a big stop on Jayson Tatum.

The Hawks turned the ball over, but the Celtics gave it right back to them with seconds remaining, and they fouled Alexander-Walker, which sent him to the free-throw line. He made both free throws, and it gave the Hawks a four-point lead. The Celtics didn't call a timeout from there, ultimately accepting defeat, and the Hawks advanced to the knockout stage of the NBA Cup.

"It was an incredible pass and it shows that quality he's got, he's done it in training plenty of times and he's shown that quality."

Jordi Fernández went to the bench earlier than normal, with nine players logging minutes in the first quarter. It feels as if he has changed his philosophy recently, feeding more into the rhythm of the game and making changes based on that rather than a predetermined notion of how minutes are distributed.

Entering the game, the Raptors had established a reputation for doing the tiny things right, like applying ball pressure and winning the rebounding battle, but they just couldn't shoot well enough to finish close games.

However, the tone of the game shifted completely by halftime. It turned into an offensive shootout, even as Brooklyn still trailed 63-55. Randle and MPJ remained the Nets' top offensive threats, combining for 27 of Brooklyn's 55 first-half points.

At the half, both teams were shooting over 50% from the field, while the Nets shot a whopping 42.1% from 3-point range. Toronto's mark from downtown wasn't too shabby either, at 38.9%. The Nets struggled to take advantage of the freebies, though, shooting just 58.3% from the charity stripe, leaving five points on the table in an eight-point game by the break.

Brooklyn's toughest task in the first half was containing Scottie Barnes, who dropped 22 points in 17 minutes on 7-of-12 shooting, including a 2-of-4 mark from downtown. He led Toronto's offense early before finishing the night with 34 points.

It was a close game throughout the first half. Coming out of the break, though, that narrative flipped in an instant. Call it the Nets continuing to fulfill that "two-face" identity. You don't even have to look at it game by game to get that takeaway; it's quarter by quarter, as it was on Friday.

After the third quarter, Toronto led 102-79. All it took was one quarter, in which the Nets lost 39-24, to really put themselves in a tough hole after a pretty solid first half. On top of Barnes, Immanuel Quickley emerged as another offensive problem for the Nets, scoring 21 points in the third quarter, leading the Raptors' 39-point frame.

The damage was already done. Toronto maintained its 23-point advantage for most of the fourth quarter before closing out the 124-100 victory.

If you're looking for positives as a Nets fan, Mikel Brown Jr. set a career high with 21 points in 25 minutes and arguably put out his best game as a pro yet. Other than that, the lack of defense continues to crush Brooklyn, especially playing a team like Toronto that possesses offensive firepower.

Because of that, the Nets are now 4-14 on the season after Friday's loss.

Final score: Toronto Raptors 124, Brooklyn Nets 100

The Nets will evaluate Brown Jr. to see whether he'll play in his first full back-to-back.

The rookie had a career-high 21 points in 25 minutes.

It's a quick turnaround for the Nets, who head to Charlotte to play the second leg of their back-to-back tomorrow. After the Hornets tomorrow, they'll face Thunder two times in a row, Celtics, Pistons, Mavericks, Magic, Wizards, Blazers, and Spurs.

#2664. Are these three brothers British skiing's next family dynasty?

Three Britons on a skiing podium, the union jack emblazoned across their race bibs as they lift their skis in celebration.

And then you learn they all have the same surname.

At a slalom race in New Zealand in September, Luca, Freddy and Zak Carrick-Smith completed a sibling clean sweep of the medals, something no three brothers are believed to have ever done before in the history of FIS alpine skiing.

"It was super special," Freddy tells BBC Sport. "The goal is to do the same thing at a World Cup or the Olympics now."

Their success came at the start of a winter season in which the brothers hope to solidify their burgeoning potential as British alpine skiing's next big things.

And could they follow in the grooves of Olympians Graham and Martin Bell, and Alain and Noel Baxter, to become GB's next family skiing dynasty?

Freddy, 19, is on GB's World Cup squad, while his twin Zak and older brother Luca, 21, are on the second-tier Europa Cup team.

And with their parents as their coaches, it is a full family affair.

The boys' mother Emma Carrick-Anderson was a four-time Winter Olympian for Team GB, while father Phil Smith founded Snoworks ski courses, which operate across Europe.

"They know us best, so they know us much better than just a random coach would," says Zak.

"And then as brothers, me and Freddy have been racing our whole lives together, pushing each other, and then Luca ahead pushing us too. I think that's why we've got so far."

Luca adds: "The best part of it probably, for us, is the competition, and I always want to be the best in everything, especially when we grew up.

"Everything you did, you'd always be pushing harder and harder. We all get along really well, and it's just like being with your best friends all the time.

"It's always been pretty incredible, but it has been difficult at times."

Emma is matter-of-fact about that challenge. Asked what was behind the decision to go it alone as a family, she said: "Basically we didn't have a choice. Ski racing is incredibly expensive.

"When the boys were young, it was all just fun. I don't think we really planned that we were going to take this journey to where we are now, knocking on the World Cup door.

"We would never have been able to afford to put them in an academy. So I think we were lucky, I was an ex-ski racer, Phil was a ski racer, we were also ski coaches, so we could do it ourselves. Not all families are quite as lucky."

Each season, they must source about £320,000. Last season, they feared they would run out of money by mid-January.

While some of their funding comes through GB Snowsport and its Alpine Foundation, the rest must be found through sponsorship deals and crowdfunding campaigns.

When BBC Sport speaks to Emma, she is in Colorado with Freddy, where he will race in the giant slalom World Cup this weekend.

There, a two-and-a-half-hour training session on the slopes costs $1,200 (£914). Fortunately, they are able to split that cost with other teams, but with Luca in Finland and Zak in Austria, Emma and Phil - who quit their jobs a number of years ago - effectively run three different programmes.

Emma Carrick-Anderson competed at the 1992, 1994, 1998 and 2002 Winter Olympics for Great Britain [Getty Images]

Coaches, ski techs, fitness instructors, course-setters, drivers, cooks - they have done plenty of jobs on their sons' journeys up the rankings.

Emma describes them as completely different personalities, and yet "all incredibly determined in their own way". But managing the emotions of her three sons as they learn to navigate the ups and downs of professional sport has been the parents' hardest role.

"They're our kids first, so they're humans first before athletes. And I think that's so important because that will help you ride out the tough times," says Emma.

"I was an athlete myself, and it's very difficult sometimes to separate Emma from the ski racer.

"That is something I know a lot of people struggle with, but it's something that we've been really working on with our guys. You know, if you have a bad result, it doesn't matter. You're not a bad person."

Freddy Carrick-Smith celebrates after his second run in Solden [Getty Images]

Thankfully, there hasn't been much in the way of bad results for the Carrick-Smiths so far this season - and Freddy in particular has enjoyed a dream start to the winter.

In October, in the first giant slalom World Cup of the season in Solden, Austria, he finished 12th - the best-ever result by a British man in the discipline at that level.

After the first run, he was in 21st place - and so hard were his celebrations at that point that he snapped a pole.

Zak and Luca were watching his second run from the finish area, while Emma was watching from the wings and Phil from the start gate. Freddy recorded the fifth-fastest time of the day to rise nine places in the standings.

"It gives me a lot of confidence," he said. "I think I knew I had it in me, but after last year's performance in the World Cup [when he failed to qualify for the second run], I wasn't so sure.

"But I was feeling good going into the race, and I thought I could get into the top 30 and have a good second run, so I thought it was possible."

The campaign continues Stateside for Freddy this weekend in Copper Mountain. Only securing his place on the startline after his success in Solden, it is an unexpected yet welcome twist early on in the season - at an added cost of £20,000 that had not been budgeted for.

"We just keep going. You keep going, keep being positive," says Emma. "Things like Freddy's results. it just makes you realise how incredibly far we've come."

And yet they hope there is further to go. Asked about their ultimate goal, twin telepathy comes to the fore.

"We want to be the best in the world," Freddy and Zak say in unison.

#2663. Celtics lose Group C to Hawks 87-86, will be Play-In wildcard

Jalen Johnson and the Hawks' defense proved too much for the Celtics in a 87-86 loss in the final game of NBA Cup group play. Boston had a chance to lock up East Group C and home-court advantage through the semifinals of the NBA Cup's elimination rounds, but the loss allowed the Hawks to win the group via tiebreaker.

However, their record and point differential still leave the team with the wild card spot, so the team is set to face the Detroit Pistons in the quarterfinals.

Boston started Derrick White, Hugo Gonzalez, Paul George, Jayson Tatum, and Neemias Queta against Atlanta. Mitchell Robinson remained out as he recovers from COVID for the fourth straight game.

The Hawks started Kingston Flemings, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson, and Onyeka Okongwu. The team's loaded injury report included CJ McCollum, Jock Landale, Mouhamed Gueye, Asa Newell, and Henri Veesaar.

The game got going with a couple ugly offensive possessions for the C's, but Gonzalez put Boston on the scoreboard with a putback layup off a Queta miss. Luckily, the Hawks also had a rough start and missed their first 5 shot attempts of the game. Daniels was the first to break the ice for Atlanta by hitting a three-pointer from the corner, but the early game was defined by defense.

While the Celtics struggled to break free from their defenders along the perimeter, Gonzalez hit the team's first three-pointer of the game off an assist from Tatum to put Boston up 8-3. That score held for a couple minutes, as neither team could score consistently. However, the Hawks had the hardest time breaking through, as they missed 11 of their first 12 shots from the field.

BOSTON, MA – NOVEMBER 27: Dyson Daniels #5 of the Atlanta Hawks and Nickeil Alexander-Walker #7 surround Hugo Gonzalez #28 of the Boston Celtics during the second quarter of an Emirates NBA Cup group stage game at TD Garden on November 27, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. With about 6 minutes left in the quarter, the bench was subbed in to play alongside Tatum and made an immediate impact as Baylor Scheierman hit a three-pointer that was only possible due to an offensive rebound by Luka Garza, who got a layup of his own shortly after. At that point, both teams got into a better offensive rhythm. JT took a more active role on the floor and hit a couple shots, while Johnson and Luguentz Dort sunk a couple of their own. By the time Payton Pritchard finished a layup with 2:23 to go in the quarter, the Celtics were ahead 21-12.

The Hawks' perimeter defense was doing a great job at running the C's off of the line, so Boston attacked the paint early and often. That attack resulted in a solid contested layup by Tatum, who followed it up with a slick step-back three-pointer on the next trip down the court. He had 13 points in the first quarter alone.

The Celtics finished the quarter in dominant fashion, as Pritchard hit a three-pointer and the defense locked down the Hawks to end the frame.

Boston opened the second quarter with a 29-14 lead, but immediately surrendered a three-pointer and turned the ball over on their side of the court. Queta got the scoring going with an easy layup over Daniels. A couple plays later, Queta got an offensive rebound and passed it out to Sam Hauser for an open three-pointer.

That started off an impressive little stretch by Hauser, who then got an offensive rebound of his own off a missed Pritchard three-pointer and put it back for an easy layup, then stole the ball on a bad pass from Corey Kispert. However, he was subbed out soon after in favor of Ron Harper Jr.

The Hawks scored a quick 5 points to narrow Boston's lead to 37-25, and had a chance to cut it to 10, but White got a nice block on Okongwu and got it ahead to George for a transition layup and his first points of the game. Unfortunately for George, he racked up 4 turnovers over his first 12 minutes of play and was subbed out with a little more than 6 minutes to go in the frame.

BOSTON, MA – NOVEMBER 27: Jayson Tatum #0 of the Boston Celtics drives to the basket during the game against the Atlanta Hawks during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 27, 2026 at TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. Tatum came back into the game around the same time and hit another contested layup to put the C's up 43-30 with less than 5 minutes to go in the half, but Boston looked a little sloppy and called a timeout about a minute later.

Following the break, Tatum missed a tough shot but got immediate redemption with a steal that led to a Gonzalez transition layup. Gonzalez also hit a beautiful floater while driving down the lane a couple plays later. While White masterfully broke up a fast break by the Hawks, Atlanta's offense clearly started clicking before halftime. They scored 9 points over the final 3 minutes of the half, which finished with the C's up 51-39.

At halftime, Tatum had 16 points — which led the team — on 54.5% shooting from the field, along with 4 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 steals.

No other Celtic finished the first half with double-digit points, but Gonzalez wasn't far behind with 9 points on 4-6 shooting. Queta had only 3 points, but was incredibly active on the boards, as he racked up 12 rebounds.

On the Hawks' side of things, Johnson led the way with 12 points (on 4-12 shooting), 7 rebounds, 2 assists, and 3 stocks. Like Tatum, he was the only player on his team to finish with double-digit points.

Overall, the half closed with the Celtics shooting 50% from the field and 40% from three-point range, while the Hawks shot 28.9% from the field and 19.2% on three-pointers. However, Atlanta put up 7 more field goal attempts than Boston and 11 more three-point attempts.

Coming out of the half, White got a nice steal, but George's off night continued as he missed an open three-pointer. The Hawks capitalized and started the second half with a much stronger offensive showing than the C's. They went on a 9-4 run to cut the lead to 7 points less than 2:30 into the third quarter, with Johnson scoring 7 of Atlanta's 9 points during the stretch.

That's when George finally woke up. He hit two three-pointers over the course of three offensive possessions to bring Boston's lead back up to 13 points but, unfortunately for the Celtics, everyone else went cold. Tatum missed an easy, wide-open corner three-pointer, and White missed another open 3 the next time down, leading Head Coach Joe Mazzulla to call a timeout the next time the C's got the ball.

It didn't help much, though. While Hauser was subbed in for White, the Celtics could not buy a shot from deep. On the other hand, the Hawks scored 10 of the first 12 points scored out of the break and cut the lead down to 5, 65-60, with less than 4 minutes to go in the third quarter — leading Boston to call another timeout.

When play resumed, Garza cut into the paint for a nice layup, but the C's surrendered a three-pointer to Johnson and another to Aaron Wiggins a few plays later. By the time Kispert cut in for an easy layup with 1:30 to go in the frame, the lead had been chipped down to 69-68.

Daniels gave the Hawks their first lead of the night with a floater with 12 seconds to go, and Tatum missed a layup to end the quarter. Atlanta finished the frame with a 70-69 lead.

The Celtics still looked disjointed as the fourth quarter began, but White got a steal and knocked down a layup to put Boston on top again — at least until Dort hit a couple free throws to retake the lead. Pritchard hit a good-looking floater, but it was negated by a shot clock violation. Thankfully, he hit a step-back three-pointer from the top of the arc soon after to tie the game up at 74 with about 10 minutes left in the game.

Nevertheless, the momentum remained in the Hawks' favor, as Dort hit a three-pointer and drew a charge on Garza, which was upheld after a ridiculously long official review. The failed challenge left the C's with 2 timeouts with 9 minutes left to go.

With the help of a Queta free throw and a Hauser three-pointer, the C's took a 78-77 lead with 7:48 remaining. Tatum was subbed back in soon after, but he struggled to get the offense going again. On one play, Boston got multiple offensive boards, but missed all three shot attempts of the possession. On top of that, the refs were stingy with the whistle and called offensive fouls on both Queta and George, ending 2 possessions prematurely.

Fortunately for the Celtics, the Hawks offense also came back down to earth, and a few minutes passed without any scoring on either side. The next points weren't scored until the 4:38 mark of the fourth quarter, when Okongwu hit a floater to put the Hawks up 79-78. The Hawks got the next bucket on a Johnson dunk and took a 3-point lead with 4:06 to go.

Turnovers were killer. Queta, who was dominant on the boards and set a new personal record of 21 rebounds with 3 minutes left in the game, turned the ball over twice in quick succession. Tatum then lost his handle and lost a ball out of bounds.

The Celtics didn't score again until Dort fouled White, who knocked down a pair of free throws to narrow the Hawks' lead to 83-81 with 1:42 left in the game. White then hit a floater on the next offensive possession to tie the game at 83 with 1:10 to go.

Alexander-Walker followed up White's buckets with a driving dunk to retake the lead for Atlanta, and Johnson blocked Tatum on a drive into paint to prevent the tying bucket. With 11.9 seconds remaining and the Hawks with the ball, Tatum got a steal but turned the ball over again right after. Alexander-Walker sealed the game with a pair of free throws that put Atlanta up 87-83 with 3 seconds left to go. White hit a buzzer-beating three-pointer in the remaining time, but it wasn't enough to get the win

Tatum finished the game with 20 points on 36.4% shooting from the field, 9 rebounds, 5 assists, and 4 steals.

Queta racked up 11 points, 22 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 stocks.

On the Hawks' side, Johnson finished with 24 points and 12 rebounds, while Alexander-Walker finished with 20 points and a couple crucial last-minute plays.

The Celtics will play Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs next at 4 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 29, at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio.

#2661. Brock Purdy ruled out vs. Seahawks. Can Mac Jones carry 49ers offense?

The San Francisco 49ers will be without their quarterback for the first of their two-game NFC West leg this week.

Brock Purdy has been ruled out for their Week 12 divisional matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, head coach Kyle Shanahan announced on Friday, Nov. 27. Mac Jones will get the start at home against the defending Super Bowl champions.

Purdy sprained his left ankle in the second quarter of the Mexico City game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 22, though he kept playing and finished with 255 passing yards and three touchdowns in a 35-10 win to push the Niners' NFL-best record to 9-1. He did not practice all week while nursing his ankle and despite Shanahan's optimism that he wouldn't miss time, Purdy is now being shut down for the week after it was revealed he suffered a mid-ankle sprain, which typically is slower to heal.

Shanahan told reporters Friday that Purdy won't require surgery. Does he expect his franchise QB back next week against the Los Angeles Rams?

"It's too soon, but I mean I'm pretty optimistic about it," he said. "But I was (optimistic) about this week to start and then it changes, so hopefully it'll be all right."

Without Purdy, the Niners have been in good hands with Jones, who went 5-3 in eight games started a year ago when Purdy went down with a toe injury. In those eight games, Jones threw 13 touchdowns for 2,151 yards with six interceptions and a 97.4 passer rating.

The Seahawks, on the other hand, are no stranger to quarterback injuries this year. They'll have Sam Darnold back on Sunday from a quad injury that kept him out of their last two games.

Though the 49ers are tied with the Chicago Bears for most wins in the league with nine, these next two divisional games against the third-place Seahawks and second-place Rams will be crucial as they lead LA by 2 1/2 games in the ultracompetitive NFC West.

#2658. Mike McCarthy admits he hasn't spent enough time with the defense

After registering an unlikely 27-5 win over the previously 8-2 Broncos, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy wasn’t angry, resentful, or defiant.

He was the same guy he always is, and he admitted that (as former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said this week), McCarthy hasn’t been sufficiently invested in the side of the ball that isn’t his personal expertise.

“I have not spent enough time with the defense,” McCarthy told reporters. “You know, and that’s something that, as far as job responsibility, job description, you know, these are things that’ll be looked at in the offseason. But, you know, it’s a point in our year where we’re making adjustments and definitely conscientious of it. But at the end of the day, we have to all do our jobs and make sure we’re giving the players the plan and all the other things that they need that we can perform and play with that type of urgency, physicality that we played today.”

McCarthy prefaced his comments with a lesson he learned as a boy, growing up in Pittsburgh.

“My father used to tell me all the time as a kid, ‘You tell the truth, you only have to tell your story once,’” McCarthy said.

The truth is that this week has entailed two sharply different versions of reality, where both things can indeed be the truth. One, McCarthy (like all of us) has flaws. Two, Rodgers should not have spoken about them publicly.

Rodgers clumsily defended his decision to break the code of a football locker room by texting this to Al Michaels: “The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.”

That’s fine, but how does disregarding the “sanctity” of the locker room (a word Rodgers undoubtedly selected in response to Tom Brady using it on Thursday) create “accountability”? McCarthy is accountable to team owner Art Rooney II. Not to the media or the fans.

And to what end? He was either doing it to help the Steelers save their season, or he was lashing out.

We’ll let you decide which explanation is more likely.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2655. Aaron Rodgers calls out Tom Brady for comments on locker room ‘sanctity’

Aaron Rodgers appeared to call out Tom Brady's "sanctity of an NFL locker room" comment in a text to Al Michaels that the Prime Video play-by-play broadcaster read during the Steelers' win over the Broncos on Friday.

"A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room, [Rodgers] said, 'The code of sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership,'" Michaels said, reading the message from Rodgers, which also included a claim that he was "barred" from the Pittsburgh facility.

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) looks to pass against the Indianapolis Colts in Pittsburgh, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. Getty Images

Rodgers drew the criticism of Brady — and numerous analysts around the NFL — after his appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, during which he accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, breaking down a halftime huddle with "1-2-3 Packers" and missing walkthroughs. The comments followed the Steelers' decision to start Rudolph and make Rodgers inactive, which they announced Tuesday night.

And while Rodgers never referenced Brady by name in his message to Michaels, the "sanctity" line was the exact phrase that the former Patriots and Buccaneers star used.

Former NFL player Tom Brady looks on prior to a game between the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers in Minneapolis, Sunday, Dec. 29, 2024. Getty Images

"The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place," Brady said Thursday on the Fox broadcast. "We shouldn't ever lose track of that as players. It's a privilege to be in that locker room. You're fighting with your teammates, you're fighting with your coaches, you're always acting as a team together. Shouldn't always be the place for private things to become public, that's what I'll say."

Brady overlapped with Rodgers in the NFL for most of his career before shifting into broadcasting after retirement, and it's unclear if Rodgers might need to contemplate a similar move after he was released by the Steelers on Wednesday.

The 42-year-old cleared waivers, but according to Prime Video reporter and NFL insider James Palmer on Thursday, teams have expressed little to no interest in signing Rodgers for the remainder of the season.

And for one night, the Steelers thrived without Rodgers, as a pair of defensive touchdowns and one touchdown pass from Rudolph improved their record to 7-4.

#2654. Grant Nelson making impact amid Nets injuries

TORONTO — There is an NBA axiom about staying ready so one doesn't have to get ready. It's what Grant Nelson has been doing this season, really, the past two, with G League Long Island, awaiting his chance with Brooklyn.

That chance arrived with the Nets' big man woes that saw Nelson — who had five rebounds and four assists in a 124-100 loss to the Raptors on Friday — finally called up.

Brooklyn's struggles at the backup center spot, bottoming out with Moritz Wagner's knee injury, have given Nelson his opportunity. And he's cashed in to give the Nets some much-needed hustle.

"Just being [ready], staying ready, being out in Long Island under those coaches, just learning the system throughout the two years I've been here., being out in Long Island under those coaches, just learning the system throughout the two years I've been here. And when my name was called, being ready," Nelson said. "So, it's just great all the preparation that I put in, finally seeing that unfold on the basketball court. And it's just good to be with this team, get some minutes."

Grant Nelson walks down court during the Emirates NBA Cup Group Play against the Milwaukee Bucks at Fiserv Forum on Nov. 25, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Getty Images

Nelson, 24, got the call-up at the start of the Nets' four-game road trip, making his season debut in a brief cameo at Minnesota. But when Wagner, one of just two proven centers on Brooklyn's roster, left with knee soreness Wednesday in Milwaukee, that's when the 6-foot-10 Nelson had an opportunity to step up.

In the first meaningful non-tanking minutes of his career, Nelson actually helped the Nets to a 104-97 victory. He had just one point but added six rebounds, including three on the offensive glass, and was a plus-six in 13:04.

"You saw Grant: You plug him in, and he does everything well. His size, how smart he is, skilled, tough — really, really tough," head coach Jordi Fernández said. "And since we've had him here, he's been himself, and he's a very, very good basketball player. He was a big reason why we won. You see the rebounding and the activity and the physicality defensively, and I expect him just to play hard."

Of all the things Nelson did, playing hard was the most important. It's something that stood out on a Nets team that hasn't done it enough.

"He's just coming in and playing as hard as he can. He's not gonna be perfect and not make mistakes, but he makes up for it with effort," Julius Randle said. "He's just doing all the little things, the dirty work, the things that we need to win that might not show up on the stat sheet. So he's playing really hard, playing with a lot of good energy, and it's contagious."

Grant Nelson (16) and Egor Demin (8) play defense during the game against the Toronto Raptors during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on Nov. 27, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

For a Brooklyn team that has shown a disappointing lack of hustle and energy, Nelson provided plenty.

He led the team in Defensive Rating, Offensive Rebound percentage and box outs, with five of the latter. For perspective, the rest of the Nets combined for just six while the Bucks finished with seven.

Nelson was an undrafted 2025 rookie, and other than four NBA cameos he spent the season in the G-League working at forward and center. But this year he was exclusively a center, averaging 16.8 points and 11.8 boards on 57.4 percent shooting before getting called up.

"Continuing to work on my game, still making that transition to a five man, so being able to guard in the perimeter, still working on that jump shot. I've taken a step this year getting rebounds, so just doing that at this next level," Nelson said. "Just continuing to be able to guard ball screens, guard guards, being able to switch onto them when I have to. And then being in every action offensively and defensively, having the conditioning for that and being physical with the fives.

"How I move kind of gives me an advantage. So continuing to be able to move my feet defensively on guards.So continuing to be able to move my feet defensively on guards. … I feel like I still have a lot to work on, but just continuing to show that."

#2652. Arizona volleyball ends season with 5-set loss on senior night

After advancing to the postseason the last two seasons, the Arizona Wildcats had to find new things to celebrate as this volleyball season wound to an end with the postseason long since out of reach. A win at home on senior night could have been one of those things, but the final match of the season was a microcosm of the season as a whole.

Arizona played streaks of high-level volleyball, but it could not do it consistently enough to win. After two sets of near-perfect play and a 2-0 lead, the Wildcats collapsed. Kansas State completed a 3-2 (25-27, 16-25, 25-19, 25-17, 19-17) reverse sweep. It ended in the most anticlimactic way possible with a center line violation called on Arizona.

"I think we got too lax and thought they were going to roll over, even though we know they had gone to multiple five sets," said Arizona head coach Rita Stubbs. "And then we didn't know how to respond once we took our foot off the gas. Immature."

Both the home and the visiting Wildcats have had disappointing seasons this year after going to the NCAA Tournament last year. K-State came in with 13-12 overall record and 5-12 record in the Big 12. UA was searching for its third conference win and the first against someone other than last-place Texas Tech. Instead, Arizona ends 7-22 overall and 2-16 in league play.

Arizona's outside hitters both had superb outings. Destiny Ndam-Simpson already had a career high 20 kills before the third set was over. She ended with 28 kills on .260 hitting. She had a double-double with 13 digs. She added four assists, an ace, and one total block.

Carlie Cisneros also had a double-double. The junior outside hitter contributed 18 kills and 20 digs. She had an assist, an ace, and three total blocks.

Cisneros was especially critical after Arizona dropped the third and fourth sets then fell behind 6-1 in the fifth. KSU was over a third of the way to a set victory, but the home Wildcats fought back to take a 10-9 lead. Eventually, they had four match points. Two of them were earned off kills by Cisneros, including one on an assist from Ndam-Simpson.

"I think Carlie put the team on her back a little bit and said, 'I'm going for it,'" Stubbs said. "This one ball—and I said it to [the team]—that Harmony [Sample] set, set it on the complete opposite side, and Carlie saw it and went up and blocked instead of backing off. You know, it was like those plays put you in a position to be ready to go and be aggressive."

Between the end of the second set and midway through the fifth, Arizona just couldn't find that aggression often enough. The team had 20 kills in a hard-fought first set. It followed with 18 in a set that it dominated. After that, it was 12 and 10 in sets that K-State controlled. The 12 the UA Wildcats had in the 15-point fifth set equaled or bettered what they had in the two 25-point sets preceding it.

"As attackers, we stopped being aggressive," Stubbs said. "We were going up and swinging at everything in the first set. I mean, we had 20 kills in the first set and 18 in the second. Then we went down to 12, and so clearly not being aggressive. And then the serve and pass game stumped us a little bit. And even when we got a good pass, we were then lax again on defense, whereas we should have been going."

Arizona played hard-scrambling defense for the first two sets. The team seemed to let nothing hit the floor while also out-blocking the opponent.

The home Wildcats had a considerable advantage in almost every stat—kills, hitting percentage, digs, and blocks—when the score reached 15-7 in the second set. By the end of the match, KSU was just a hair behind in kills and hitting percentage. The visiting Wildcats took the advantage in both digs and blocks.

K-State started the match better than Arizona did. KSU was up by five at 12-7, but Arizona went on a 7-2 run to tie it. Cisneros and Ndam-Simpson each had three kills during the run.

Arizona didn't take a lead until 20-19. It reached set point at 24-22 only to have KSU win the next three points to get its own set point at 25-24.

Stubbs called time and her team responded. Three straight kills by Ndam-Simpson had Arizona up 1-0.

It carried over into the second set, which Arizona led wire-to-wire. The biggest lead came at 21-10, and UA cruised to a relatively easy win.

K-State flipped the script in the third set. The purple Wildcats never trailed. Their biggest lead came at 19-11. Arizona used a 5-0 run to get within three points, but KSU just needed to trade runs to extend the match.

The fourth set was effectively over when KSU went on a 7-0 run to take a 10-3 lead. Arizona never won more than two points in a row as the visiting team forced the short set.

It turned out to be longer than expected. Arizona didn't go away when KSU got a 6-1 lead in the fifth. It cut into the advantage a little at a time then used a 5-0 run to take the lead.

From there, it was a back-and-forth affair. Arizona reached match point at 15-14. It had another at 16-15. A third came at 17-16. Kansas State saved them all.

Finally, K-State earned its first match point at 18-17. As Arizona scrambled to keep a ball up, the whistle blew. The home Wildcats were called for a center line violation. A review confirmed it. The match and season were over in the most frustrating way possible.

The Wildcats celebrated middle blocker Journey Tucker, opposite Britt Carlson, and outside hitter Payton Woods before the match. Tucker has been at Arizona for four years and has been a starter for much of that time. Carlson came to Tucson two years ago after stints at Washington State and UCF. Woods joined this season after time at Virginia Tech, Mississippi State, and Sam Houston State.

Tucker's mother moved out of state during her daughter's time in college. She hadn't been to Tucson in a while, but she made senior day.

"It meant a lot for my family to come down here and watch my senior game," Tucker said. "It meant a lot, and I'm super happy. It was my sister's first time seeing me play in a while, so I'm also happy about that. It's just truly a blessing that they took the time out here to come and watch me in person. I always get texts from them about watching me on TV, so for them to come for our last game and see me in person, it means a lot to me."

Tucker got a fifth season when the NCAA implemented age-based eligibility over the summer. Early in the season, she said that she had already spoken to Stubbs about the possibility of coming back for her fifth season as a Wildcat. Those plans no longer seem so firm.

"Still up in the air about my fifth year," Tucker said. "So just really weighing out all my options and just continuing to talk to my coaches and things like that. So you never know what's going to happen. I think luckily I'm still going to be here in the spring to finish my degree."

Being here in the spring would mean the opportunity to practice with the team even if she plans to transfer, but that would depend on the coaching staff.

Three years ago, Sofia Maldonado Diaz practiced with Arizona during the spring despite being in the transfer portal and actively visiting other programs. That is a rarity, but it is something Stubbs has allowed for at least one player who was leaving on good terms with the program. Like Tucker, Maldonado Diaz was with the program for four years and graduated from Arizona.

Tucker plays a premium position. Middle blockers with good size are always valued. She came into the match tied for third in the Big 12 in blocks per set. She's someone who would likely get a good deal of attention—and probably revenue share money that Arizona cannot match—if she opts to go into the portal. She has also completed the four years she thought she was going to get when she first committed to Arizona.

It would be a big blow for Arizona to lose her. The Wildcats lost their other starting middle blocker after last season. She transferred to Miami, which is closer to home. It had Stubbs searching for another one in the portal.

There is a middle blocker in the incoming freshman class, but she has been injured for two years. Arizona also has both Kristen Dear and Marina Vosloo on the roster, assuming that both are committed to returning, but neither has the experience or blocking acumen that Tucker does. That blocking acumen accounted for an outsized portion of Arizona's scoring this season.

#2650. Spurs erase 20-point deficit to eliminate Lakers in NBA Cup action, advance to knockout round as wild card

The most wide-open division of the 2026 NBA Cup entering Friday, the final day of group play, was West Group C, which had four different teams capable of clinching a spot in the knockout rounds. Two of those teams were the San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers, and they delivered one of the night's wildest games.

The Spurs erased a 20-point deficit on their way to a 99-96 win over the Lakers, riding another huge game from Victor Wembanyama. The win officially put them in the knockout rounds as the West's wild card, thanks to a plus-57 point differential in four games.

Simultaneously, the Portland Trail Blazers won the group by defeating the Golden State Warriors and holding the tiebreaker over San Antonio. The Lakers and Warriors were eliminated with the losses.

Wembanyama finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, 4 steals, 2 assists and 2 blocks, but his 3-for-8 night at the line also invited disaster toward the end of the game, when the Lakers were trying to inch their way back into it.

Los Angeles got the ball down three with a chance to tie the game twice in the final 10 seconds, but the Spurs fouled both times and managed to hold on for the win.

It was a brutal first half for the Spurs, who entered halftime down 54-38, but they proceeded to outscore the Lakers 30-14 in the third quarter and continued that momentum into the fourth quarter to take control.

It's a return to knockout-round action for the Spurs, who reached the NBA Cup championship game last year before losing to the New York Knicks (a result that was repeated in the NBA Finals). They will now face the Dallas Mavericks, the only team to go undefeated in group play, in the quarterfinals next week.

#2647. Steelers WR DK Metcalf clarifies he wasn't shouting out Aaron Rodgers via sign language after scoring TD

In case you somehow haven't heard, Aaron Rodgers was not playing for the Pittsburgh Steelers during their game on Black Friday. That doesn't mean he didn't come up.

Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf, one of Rodgers' closest teammates during his time in Pittsburgh, appeared to shout out the quarterback after scoring a touchdown in the first quarter against the Denver Broncos. After catching the 22-yard pass from new starter Mason Rudolph, viewers noted Metcalf making a series of hand signals.

The popular translation via American Sign Language: "Stand on business, eight." Eight was Rodgers' jersey number with the Steelers.

That, however, turned out to not be the case. After the game, Metcalf told Brendan Howe of Steelers Now that he was actually declaring "Keep standing on business, four." Four is Metcalf's jersey number.

The video shows Metcalf holding up four fingers on both hands, hence the apparent confusion.

Pittsburgh entered the game carrying some very public baggage, after their starting quarterback burned every bridge in sight on his way out. The Steelers responded with a dominant performance — including two defensive touchdowns in the first half — thumping the Denver Broncos 27-5. Metcalf caught three passes for 36 yards and the touchdown in the win.

DJ Metcalf caught a touchdown pass from one quarterback then sent a message to another.

The trouble reportedly began when Rodgers made some sort of "ultimatum," as Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy put it, on Tuesday, which the team did not heed. Instead, Pittsburgh opted to bench Rodgers and start Rudolph against Denver, which led to Rodgers appearing on his friend Pat McAfee's show on ESPN on Wednesday and unleashing a torrent of grievances against McCarthy. The Steelers released Rodgers not long after.

Even more details were provided during the game Friday, as broadcaster Al Michaels shared the contents of a text from Rodgers, who claimed McCarthy ghosted him until the benching was announced and that the Steelers barred him from the facilities on Wednesday.

A larger question to come out of the dispute was how the rest of the Steelers players would respond to a dispute between quarterback and head coach. A lopsided win was a decent sign the team wasn't tearing itself apart.

#2646. Lobos Make History, Beat Air Force 42-19 to Clinch First-Ever Mountain West Championship Game

ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) –The University of New Mexico football team continues to make history. With a 42-19 victory over Air Force, the Lobos secured their first-ever appearance in the Mountain West Championship Game and earned the opportunity to host the title matchup.

New Mexico's defense set the tone early against the Falcons. Brett Karhu made an early impact with a tackle for loss, while Tavian Combs intercepted Air Force quarterback Evan Medders during the Falcons' second drive, returning it 17 yards.

The turnover helped spark the Lobos' offense. Kiefer Sibley took advantage, breaking through contact and racing 52 yards for a touchdown to tie the game at seven in the first quarter.

Sibley led New Mexico with 115 rushing yards, while Ricklan Holmes added a touchdown late in the opening quarter to help the Lobos take a 14-7 lead. New Mexico continued to find success on the ground and carried a 21-13 advantage into halftime.

The passing game took over in the second half, led by quarterback Luke Moga. He finished with 248 passing yards and three touchdown passes, including two in the second half.

One of those scores came on a connection with Bailen George, who turned on the speed for another Lobos touchdown. George finished with 100 receiving yards and two touchdowns.

New Mexico also held Air Force scoreless in the fourth quarter and finished with a 182-162 advantage in rushing yards.

The 42-19 win gives the Lobos their 10th victory of the season, tying the program record for most wins in a single season.

Moga said the offense still has room to improve despite the big performance.

"I just went out there and let it rip. I know there's definitely some throws I wanted tonight, too. He could've had probably 140 if I would've hit him on an over [route]. So there's definitely things to clean up. We're not even close to perfect, and we've got a chance next week to be as close to perfect as we can be," Moga said.

Head coach Jason Eck praised his team's performance but emphasized the importance of the opportunity ahead.

"They're a good football team, but we've got a really good football team there. And again, we want to go win this game next week and stake our claim to be the best Lobo team ever, which is saying something. We've been playing football over 100 years here," Eck said.

New Mexico will host the Mountain West Championship Game on Friday, December 4, at 7 p.m. The game will air on FOX.

#2645. Lakers go cold in second half and lose to the Spurs

Victor Wembanyama slammed a reverse two-handed dunk over Walker Kessler. On the next play, he volleyball spiked Collin Sexton's layup attempt into the front row at Frost Bank Center. San Antonio fans wagged their index fingers toward the court.

The "MVP" chants that so often greet Luka Doncic even in visiting arenas belong to the Spurs' French superstar here.

Wembanyama's 25 points and 16 rebounds led the Spurs to a 99-96 comeback win over the Lakers on Friday in a thrilling matchup between the top two teams in the Western Conference. The Lakers (15-4) squandered a 20-point first-half lead that cost them a spot in the NBA Cup knockout round. Instead of advancing to the quarterfinals of the in-season tournament, the Lakers will play two regular-season matchups in two weeks.

The quarterfinals on Dec. 4-5 are set: Boston-Detroit, Philadelphia-Atlanta, San Antonio-Dalla, Memphis-Portland.

Doncic had 31 points, eight assists and six rebounds, but he continues to struggle on three-point shots. He entered Friday's game shooting 26.6% from three during the last five games and went just one for 13 from beyond the arc in the much-anticipated showdown.

The Lakers, who led by 20 with 4:43 left in the second quarter and 16 at halftime, got an uneven return from Austin Reaves. The guard who missed the last five games because of a left heel bruise had 21 points and eight rebounds with seven turnovers, but was held to just two points in the first half. He scored 13 in the fourth quarter, including a three with 34 seconds to go that brought the Lakers to within three before the Spurs inched away from the free-throw line.

Lakers guard Luka Doncic, putting up a shot against Spurs guard Dylan Harper, finished with 31 points on Friday night but only made one of 13 three-point shots. (Ronald Cortes / Getty Images)

The Lakers went 4-1 without Reaves and remained atop the NBA standings entering Friday. But the Lakers lead the league with outside skepticism. They had only played eight games against teams currently better than .500. They hadn't played a winning team since narrowly surviving a comeback attempt from the Atlanta Hawks on the road on Nov. 9. Three games — at San Antonio, Memphis and Houston — on their current four-game trip could serve as early statement opportunities.

The Lakers looked every bit the championship contenders they hoped to be during the first half. They ended the first quarter on an 8-0 run that chewed up more than four minutes. Despite Doncic struggling with his three-point shot early, missing his first six shots from distance, he still orchestrated the Lakers to a 13-point first-quarter lead.

The Lakers fought to keep the Spurs (16-4) scoreless even when playing without Kessler against Wembanyama. The French superstar got swarmed by Jarred Vanderbilt, Sandro Mamukelashvili and even switched onto 6-foot-5 guard Quentin Grimes yet was held to just two points and three rebounds during the first quarter.

With the Lakers clogging the paint, Wembanyama was forced to move outside. He made the Spurs' first three-pointer of the game, ending the team's 0-for-10 start from beyond the arc with 2:57 remaining in the second quarter. The Spurs were the third-best three-point shooting team in the league entering Friday's game at 33.4%, but were held to a season-low 38 first-half points.

They nearly equaled that total in a dominant third quarter in which they outscored the Lakers 30-14. The Spurs made three-of-eight threes during the quarter and tied the score on a corner three from Keldon Johnson with two seconds left.

The reigning Western Conference champions led the league with 48.4 rebounds per game but got outrebounded during the first half 24-15. The Spurs won the rebounding battle 47-43 and got the dagger three-pointer from Stephon Castle with 43 seconds remaining off an offensive rebound after a missed free throw by Wembanyama. Instead of a chance to tie the score, the Lakers got the ball back down by six.

#2643. Spurs rally to beat Lakers, advance in NBA Cup

The San Antonio Spurs erased a 20-point deficit to beat the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 on Friday and punch their ticket to the NBA Cup quarter-finals on the final night of group play.

Victor Wembanyama scored 25 points and grabbed 16 rebounds, adding two assists, four steals and a pair of blocked shots to fuel the Spurs in the battle between the Western Conference's top two teams.

Luka Doncic scored 31 points to lead the Lakers, but Los Angeles were eliminated from the in-season tournament.

San Antonio advanced as a wild card with a win that allowed Portland -- 116-94 winners over the Golden State Warriors --- to clinch the victory in West group C.

Seven of the eight quarter-final Cup berths were still up for grabs going into Friday's games.

The Spurs left it late, but after scoring just 38 points in the first half they out-scored the Lakers 30-14 in the third quarter to turn the tide.

Stephon Castle led San Antonio's scoring with 26 points, coming up with a pair of big three-pointers in the fourth quarter. De'Aaron Fox and Wembanyama drained clutch free throws in the waning seconds to seal the win.

"We're battle tested," Castle said. "We win big games and we stick together when it's tough for us."

In the quarter-finals the Spurs will play the Dallas Mavericks, who beat the Phoenix Suns 113-109 to finish 4-0 in group play.

The Trail Blazers will take on the Memphis Grizzlies, who beat Minnesota 114-109 to eliminate the Timberwolves.

In the East, LeBron James scored 21 points with seven rebounds and six assists as the Philadelphia 76ers cruised to a 111-87 victory over the Indiana Pacers and into the knockout rounds.

Joel Embiid scored 14 points and pulled down 11 rebounds for the Eastern Conference leading 76ers, who finished top of East group B and were joined in the quarter-finals by the Detroit Pistons, Atlanta Hawks and Boston Celtics.

Philadelphia never trailed, leading by as many as 32 to reach the Cup quarter-finals for the first time.

"We're in it," said James, who won the inaugural edition of the tournament with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2023. "Everyone knows about the Cup games, and everyone knows the importance of it and trying to play for something."

In Detroit, Isaiah Joe scored 22 points off the bench to lead seven Pistons players to score in double figures in a 113-98 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks, who led by 16 points early.

Detroit, missing starters Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson and Cade Cunningham, seized control for good with a 42-point third period and finished top of East Group A.

Atlanta clinched East group C with an 87-86 victory over the Boston Celtics -- who advanced as a wild card.

Jalen Johnson scored 24 points and Nickeil Alexander-Walker added 20 for the Hawks, who rallied from a 17-point first-half deficit on their way to a fifth straight win.

It was knotted at 83-83 with 1:10 remaining, but Alexander-Walker drove for a go-ahead basket, Jalen Johnson blocked a Jayson Tatum attempt in the lane and the Hawks held on.

Absent from the East's quarter-final lineup are the Knicks, who won last year's Cup in what proved a warm-up for their first NBA title in 53 years.

Needing a win and for other results to fall their way, the Knicks erased a 23-point deficit to lead by one in the fourth quarter before falling 108-105 to the Miami Heat.

#2642. 5 quick hitters with Silver and Black Pride: Browns’ offense can take advantage of Raiders’ interior

This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns return from their bye at home as they take on the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 12. To help preview a few topics from the Raiders' perspective, we reached out to Matt Holder from Silver and Black Pride and exchanged five questions with him.

Chris: "The Raiders are a big draw to watch again (at least to me) with Fernando Mendoza now starting. How have things looked for the first overall pick through two games?"

Matt: "Mendoza has certainly had his ups and downs over the last two weeks, as facing off against the Seahawks' and Broncos' defenses are brutal opponents to get your feet wet as a starting quarterback in the NFL. He had some issues deciphering Mike Macdonald's complex pressure looks and has taken way too many sacks (11) over the last couple of weeks. However, I thought he did a better job of feeling pressure and navigating the pocket in Denver. The Broncos were just able to get to him later in the game when the Raiders were trailing, and Denver's pass-rushers could pin their ears back.

Dawgs By Nature is SB Nation's home for Browns news, analysis, and conversation. Download the app to connect with fellow Cleveland diehards and share your take.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

One thing that Mendoza has brought to the offense is the ability to create off-script plays, which is ironic because that was viewed as one of his weaknesses coming out of Indiana. Don't get me wrong, Kirk Cousins did a great job operating the offense, but the 38-year-old's limited mobility and arm strength made it difficult for the offense to get out of bad situations. Meanwhile, the rookie has used his legs as a weapon, either by taking off and running or scrambling and making some impressive throws on the run. The clip below (link) highlights a few plays/throws that simply weren't happening with Cousins at quarterback.

So, there have definitely been some rookie struggles over the last two weeks. But the traits that made the No. 1 pick the No. 1 pick have shown up, and everyone in Raider Nation should be really excited about the future despite Mendoza being 0-2 as a starter so far."

Chris: "What do you view as the Raiders' biggest weakness on defense right now?"

Matt: "The defensive tackle position, and it's not particularly close.

Everyone knew Las Vegas' interior defensive line needed to be addressed in the offseason, but general manager John Spytek didn't add a defensive tackle until the seventh round of the draft. Now, according to Pro Football Focus, the Raiders' defensive tackle who has the highest pass-rush win rate (Thomas Booker IV at 8.6 percent) ranks 54th at the position among players with at least 74 pass-rush snaps.

Additionally, the two best run defenders at the position — Foley Fatukasi and Tim Keenan III — weren't even on the roster to begin training camp. Fatukasi had been available as a free agent for about six months before getting signed after the Raiders' first preseason game, while Keenan was a seventh-round pick by the Rams before failing to make Los Angeles' roster and getting added to Las Vegas' practice squad. To clarify, Keenan has played in the last five games and was added to the active roster a couple of weeks ago. As a result, the Raiders are allowing the second-most rushing yards per game (149.5) and are third-to-last in yards per carry allowed (4.8).

Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard is trying to run a variation of Macdonald's defense in Seattle, but Leonard simply doesn't have the talent on the interior of the defensive line that the Seahawks have to properly execute it. In my opinion, that's the biggest root cause of the defensive issues in Vegas."

Chris: "Cleveland went into Las Vegas last year around this same time and terrorized Geno Smith with ten sacks, and pretty much dominated that game. Besides QB, what are the biggest differences you see between last year's team and this year's that could make for a different outcome?"

Matt: "Klint Kubiak is the biggest difference. Last year's Browns game ended up being Chip Kelly's last as offensive coordinator, with Pete Carroll firing Kelly shortly after the contest. The rumor is that Carroll was forcing Kelly to run a specific type of offense instead of letting the play caller put together his own scheme, and I can say that Kelly's offense looked nothing like I expected it to be with very generic play calling and little to no creativity.

Meanwhile, Kubiak is in full control as the head coach and offensive play-caller. Whether it's Cousins or Mendoza at quarterback, the Raiders' offensive scheme has been much better than it was a year ago. That's led to a dramatic difference in points per game, going from ranking dead last at 14.2 ppg to 11th at 25.0 ppg. Fun fact: It only took 10 games for the 2026 team to surpass the 2025 team's point total (241) for the entire season.

Also, while the Raiders' current offensive line is far from perfect, the unit is better than last year's at this point in the season. Of the six linemen who played against the Browns last year, only one remains on the current active roster: right tackle DJ Glaze, who is arguably the team's most improved player. So, while I mentioned previously that sacks were an issue for Mendoza, he's already shown growth in that area, and the line is better than it was at this point a year ago."

Chris: "Tell us about one player who Browns fans may not have heard of, but who could have an impact on this Sunday's game."

Matt: "I'm going to cheat and go with two, one on each side of the ball: wide receiver Jack Bech and safety Treydan Stukes.

Bech, the 2025 second-round pick, is coming off his best game as a pro with eight catches for 88 yards and a touchdown. Week 10 was ugly, where he had a couple of drops and was unproductive with just two grabs and 10 yards. However, Bech and Mendoza seem to have good chemistry together, as the second-year wideout leads the team with 15 targets over the last two weeks, per PFF. He isn't a great athlete who is going to generate a ton of separation on his routes, but the TCU product is good on contested targets and at finding holes in zone coverage.

Stukes, the 2026 second-round pick, has primarily been a free safety and has done well in that role. He's constantly around the ball, with a pair of interceptions, five passes defended and several quality tackles to limit gains in both the passing and running games. Recently, the coaching staff has been tapping into the Arizona product's versatility, playing him at some nickelback (his college position) and having him line up against tight ends. It wouldn't surprise me if we see Stukes and Harold Fannin Jr. face off against each other frequently on Sunday."

Chris: "The Browns are underdogs against the Raiders on Sunday (Browns -4.5 as of this question, per FanDuel). Who would you pick to win the game?"

Matt: "Call me a homer, but I kind of like the Raiders to pull off the upset. Cleveland has become known for having slow starts and making fourth-quarter comebacks so far this season, ranking 31st in first-quarter points per game (1.3) but tied for 10th in fourth-quarter ppg (7.4). Meanwhile, Las Vegas' defense has generated the most fourth-quarter turnovers (10, h/t Ari Meirov on X/Twitter), three more than any other team, and ranks 10th in ppg allowed (6.1) during the final frame.

So, I think that tilts in the Silver and Black's favor, and the numbers above remind me of the Saints game from earlier in the season, where the Raiders won as underdogs in New Orleans. I'll go 24-21 Vegas."

Thanks again to Matt for taking the time to answer my questions.

#2641. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B
